sample_unit: chatbot responses (25 questions x 3 prompt forms x 2 model versions)

links.outcome: Reading grade level of ChatGPT patient-education responses versus the NIH eighth-grade recommendation
links.effect: Version 3.5 had a significantly higher grade reading level than version 4.0 (p = 0.0002). Version 4.0 was more readable but still exceeded the NIH-recommended eighth-grade level.
links.quote: Version 4.0 offered more concise and readable information, aligning with the readability of most online medical resources despite exceeding the National Institutes of Health's (NIH's) recommended eighth-grade reading level.

unlisted_practices: Patient-friendly versus physician-level prompting to adapt chatbot response complexity
Comparing free and paid LLM versions for patient education accuracy

screen.reason: The study tests different prompt formulations (no prompting vs patient-friendly vs physician-level prompting) on ChatGPT 3.5 and 4.0 to evaluate impact on accuracy, reading level, and response length for patient education.
